First, let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255329/assets/2373daf4b5fd26f098bf90e998e2685db6a8b793e94ac9d80b08ea423cb535c0.png)

Notice that our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. If we reflect the graph over the $y$-axis, we get the same picture. This means that $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is an *even* function, and we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-a) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡a \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
